---
name: replicate-slice
description: Take one slice of a closed-source product from "unknown" to "verified clone" with this repository's harness. Use when starting a new target or a new slice of an existing target, or when resuming one.
---

# Replicate a slice

The method is target-agnostic. Everything about a target lives in `targets/<t>/`; if a step makes
you edit `harness/` or `.claude/` for one target, stop: that is a harness change, made on its own
and justified in its commit.

Read first: `docs/verification.md` (the standard), `docs/target-triage.md`, `docs/lessons.md`.

The session that follows this skill is the orchestrator. It runs the steps in order, delegates the
roles below, and stops at the human checkpoints. The method automates most of the work; a full
run on a new target with no other intervention has not been demonstrated yet.

## Roles

Permissions are enforced by structure wherever a role can run in a copy; prose and the guard hook
only add a guardrail. The table says which.

| Role         | Who                                        | Enforced by                                                   |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Builder      | `builder` agent                            | container on a copy without holdout; only `clone/` comes back |
| Breaker      | `breaker` agent                            | container on a copy; nothing comes back                       |
| Analyst      | `analyst` agent                            | copy with one spent batch only; only `analysis/` comes back   |
| Auditor      | `audit/auditor.md`, run by `audit/meta.ts` | container on a planted copy; only its findings are read       |
| Scorer       | `npm run verify` (code, never an agent)    | deterministic code; the clone runs in a separate process      |
| Recorder     | `recorder` agent, and `npm run record`     | prose and the guard (it needs the target's key, so no copy)   |
| Orchestrator | the session following this skill           | prose and the human checkpoints below                         |

## Human checkpoints

Ask, then wait, before: choosing the target and the slice; the terms-of-service check (automated
access, replication clauses); creating accounts and keys; any spending beyond the stated budget
(builds, audits); recording in mode d (a human performs the actions); re-recording an existing
fixture; editing `docs/verification.md` or `docs/target-triage.md`; publishing anything.

## Steps

0. **Triage.** Classify the recording mode (`docs/target-triage.md`): it sets the cost and the
   fidelity that can be promised. `npm run new-slice <t>` scaffolds a new target.
1. **Recon.** Use the product once with capture on; for an API, script a minimal world. Write
   `targets/<t>/RECON.md`: where computed values appear, noise, error messages, surprises.
2. **Ledger** (recorder). `rules.json`: rules with provenance `observed | documented | inferred |
mined` and a reference. Documentation seeds rules; only a fixture confirms them. No status.
3. **Probe design** (recorder, then breaker in spec mode). In `probes.ts`:
   - designed probes: per rule, a case that triggers it and a boundary case; interacting rules
     combined; each probe creates its own starting state;
   - **the distribution D** the claim will speak about, as a seeded generator with its support
     written down in plain words (dimensions, ranges, frequencies), and dev probes drawn from it;
   - for screens: walkthroughs with full capture and breadth-first explorations;
   - then the breaker reads RECON, rules and documentation (no clone yet) and proposes inputs
     the generators never draw; widen D's support with what it finds before going on.
4. **Adapter.** `adapter.ts` implements `TargetAdapter`: `probes()`, `run(probe, side)` with the
   same code on both sides, `cloneEntry` (the clone's module; the harness runs it in its own
   process) and `recordedWith()` (the target's API and SDK versions).
5. **Policy**, before any clone code. `policy.json`: generated IDs canonicalised; every weakening
   (ignore, type, tolerance, perceptual, mask) carries its reason, decided from the target's own
   noise and semantics, never to make a clone pass.
6. **Record dev** (`npm run record <t>`): every probe twice, noise kept, scrubbed, locked. Commit
   fixtures and lock alone.
7. **Pre-register a holdout batch.** Size it from the claim: with no failure, 299 cases bound the
   failure rate below 1 % at 95 %; 473 still do so with one failure, and bound it below 1 % at
   99 % with none. Write `analysis-plan*.md` (batch IDs `hold-<name>-001…`, D, size, decision
   rule), draw the seed into `holdout-seed.json`, **commit both**, then record the batch.
   Prefer a **staged** batch (`stages` in `holdout-seed.json`, IDs `hold-<name>-s1-001…`): the plan
   then names each stage and the number of failures the claim tolerates.
8. **Build** (`harness/run-builder.sh <t>`). The builder works in the agent container on a copy
   with no holdout, no seed and no git history; only `clone/` comes back.
9. **Break** (`harness/run-agent.sh breaker <t> …`). The breaker reads the clone and proposes
   inputs to make it fail. Store them as `dev-brk-` probes (adversarial, never holdout), record,
   verify, and go back to 8 until a round finds nothing or the budget is spent. Their failure
   share is reported, never used as an estimate.
10. **Measure once.** Freeze the clone in a commit, run `npm run verify <t> -- --split holdout`
    once, apply the plan's decision rule and write the entry in `measurements.md`.
    For a staged batch: `npm run verify <t> -- --sequential hold-<name> --max-failures <k>` scores
    stage by stage and stops as soon as failures exceed k. Stopping only on failure leaves the
    success criterion unchanged, and the stages never scored stay fresh for the next clone.
11. **If the claim is rejected,** the batch is spent. Run `harness/run-analyst.sh <t> <batch>`
    right after the look; turn its findings into rules and `dev-` probes (designed after seeing
    failures, so they never certify); one more build pass; then a **new batch with a new seed
    and a new plan**, and back to 10. Never fix the failures and rescore the same batch.
12. **Variance**, when the budget allows: more builds from an empty server, each in its own
    worktree, each scored once on the claim's batch; write `variance.md`. Three builds show
    reproducibility; about 29 are needed to bound how often a build misses the bar below 10 %.
13. **Audit.** `npx tsx audit/meta.ts`: planted defects, recall per run; adjudicate the other
    findings and fix the real ones.
14. **Report.** `GAPS.md` with `## Scope` and `## Measured divergences` (the fidelity report quotes
    them), the claim with its scope in the README, and a test from a fresh clone (`npm ci`,
    `npm run check`, `verify --split all`).
15. **Lessons.** Append to `docs/lessons.md` what cost time and the rule that would have saved it.

## Rules that hold across steps

- **Learn only from spent sets.** Rules, probes and prompts may change after a batch's look;
  every new claim then needs a fresh batch. Every look is logged and counted per set.
- **Prefixes decide the split:** `hold-` is always holdout, `dev-` always dev, anything else by
  hash (a quarter to holdout, which carries no claim once looked at under several clone versions).
- **Costs are logged** in `timings.jsonl` (recording, verify, every agent run); quote them.

## Re-recording

Only with evidence that the target changed or the recording was wrong (replaying the original
shows it), never because the clone fails:
`npm run record <t> -- --rerecord <id> --reason "<evidence>"`, in its own commit whose message
carries the reason and the old and new hashes the command prints.

## Claims

Fidelity is stated as "N of M" with its bound, the set's status and the distribution it holds for.
Anything without a fixture is written: "Not covered by a fixture; behaviour inferred from
<source>; unverified."
----
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs one agent headless inside the agent container, on a sandbox copy of the repository that
# holds no holdout, no audit material, no env or scrub files and no git history. The container
# sees only that copy (mounted at /work), not the host file system. The model credential comes
# from .agent.env through --env-file and is never written into the sandbox.
# Usage: harness/sandbox.sh <agent> <target> <task> [copy-back-dir]
# If copy-back-dir is given (for example targets/<t>/clone), that folder alone is copied back.
set -euo pipefail
agent="$1"
target="$2"
task="$3"
copy_back="${4:-}"
repo="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
image="software-clone-factory-agent"
credential="$repo/.agent.env"
stamp="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
log="$repo/targets/$target/logs/$agent-$stamp.jsonl"

command -v docker >/dev/null || { echo "refusing: docker is required (OrbStack or Docker Desktop)" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -f "$credential" ] || { echo "refusing: $credential is missing (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=...)" >&2; exit 2; }
docker image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1 || docker build -q -t "$image" -f "$repo/harness/docker/Dockerfile" "$repo" >/dev/null

sandbox="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/scf-sandbox-$agent-XXXX")"
egress="scf-egress-$agent-$stamp"
trap 'docker rm -f "$egress" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; rm -rf "$sandbox"' EXIT
"$repo/harness/make-sandbox.sh" "$repo" "$sandbox"

# An analyst may see one spent batch, and only one recorded as spent in measurements.md (its single
# look already taken). It goes under spent/<batch>/, out of every holdout path and pattern.
if [ -n "${SPENT_BATCH:-}" ]; then
  [[ "$SPENT_BATCH" =~ ^hold[a-z0-9-]*$ ]] || { echo "refusing: bad batch name $SPENT_BATCH" >&2; exit 2; }
  grep -q "\`${SPENT_BATCH}-001\`" "$repo/targets/$target/measurements.md" 2>/dev/null \
    || { echo "refusing: batch $SPENT_BATCH has no recorded look in measurements.md" >&2; exit 2; }
  spent="$sandbox/targets/$target/spent/$SPENT_BATCH"
  mkdir -p "$spent"
  find "$repo/targets/$target/fixtures/holdout" -name "${SPENT_BATCH}-[0-9]*.json" -exec cp {} "$spent/" \;
  jq --arg b "$SPENT_BATCH" '[.cases[] | select(.pass | not) | .id | select(test("^" + $b + "-[0-9]+$"))]' \
    "$repo/targets/$target/verify/holdout-verdict.json" >"$spent/failures.json"
fi

mkdir -p "$repo/targets/$target/logs"
# Hours of agent work must not vanish with the sandbox: the clone is copied back even when the run
# fails, and the run's status is returned at the end.
# Egress allowlist: the agent sits on an internal network with no route out; its only way out is
# a proxy container that lets through the model API (and the hosts a target lists in
# egress-allow.txt, such as its documentation) and refuses the rest, a code host included.
allow="api.anthropic.com"
if [ -f "$repo/targets/$target/egress-allow.txt" ]; then
  allow="$allow,$(grep -v '^#' "$repo/targets/$target/egress-allow.txt" | grep -v '^$' | paste -sd, -)"
fi
docker network inspect scf-internal >/dev/null 2>&1 || docker network create --internal scf-internal >/dev/null
docker run -d --rm --name "$egress" -e ALLOW="$allow" \
  -v "$repo/harness/docker/egress-proxy.mjs:/egress-proxy.mjs:ro" "$image" node /egress-proxy.mjs >/dev/null
docker network connect scf-internal "$egress"

status=0
docker run --rm \
  --env-file "$credential" -e RH_SANDBOX=1 \
  --network scf-internal \
  -e HTTPS_PROXY="http://$egress:3128" -e HTTP_PROXY="http://$egress:3128" -e NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1 \
  -e CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 \
  -v "$sandbox:/work" \
  "$image" \
  claude -p "Use the $agent subagent (Agent tool, subagent_type $agent) on target '$target' with this task, following .claude/agents/$agent.md: $task When it finishes, report its final answer verbatim." \
  --model claude-opus-5-5 \
  --permission-mode acceptEdits \
  --allowedTools "Bash Read Write Edit Grep Glob Agent WebFetch" \
  --output-format stream-json --verbose | tee "$log" | jq -rj 'select(.type == "assistant") | .message.content[]? | select(.type == "text") | .text + "\n"' || status=$?

# What the egress proxy refused, kept next to the run's log.
docker logs "$egress" 2>/dev/null | grep '^denied' >"${log%.jsonl}-egress-denied.log" || true
[ -s "${log%.jsonl}-egress-denied.log" ] || rm -f "${log%.jsonl}-egress-denied.log"

# The last line of the stream carries the run's totals: duration, turns, cost and tokens per model.
jq -c --arg agent "$agent" --arg stamp "$stamp" 'select(.type == "result")
  | {at: (now | todate), step: "agent", agent: $agent, log: ($agent + "-" + $stamp + ".jsonl"),
     seconds: (.duration_ms / 1000), turns: .num_turns, cost_usd: .total_cost_usd,
     usage: .usage, models: .modelUsage, ok: (.subtype == "success")}' "$log" \
  >>"$repo/targets/$target/timings.jsonl" || echo "warning: no result line in $log" >&2
# A build in a linked worktree is also logged in the main checkout, so its cost is never lost with it.
docker
hooks
make-sandbox.sh
run-agent.sh
run-analyst.sh
run-builder.sh
sandbox.sh

| Recorder     | `recorder` agent, and `npm run record`     | prose and the guard (it needs the target's key, so no copy)   |
| Orchestrator | the session following this skill           | prose and the human checkpoints below                         |

## Human checkpoints

Ask, then wait, before: choosing the target and the slice; the terms-of-service check (automated
access, replication clauses); creating accounts and keys; any spending beyond the stated budget
(builds, audits); recording in mode d (a human performs the actions); re-recording an existing
fixture; editing `docs/verification.md` or `docs/target-triage.md`; publishing anything.

## Steps

0. **Triage.** Classify the recording mode (`docs/target-triage.md`): it sets the cost and the
   fidelity that can be promised. `npm run new-slice <t>` scaffolds a new target.
1. **Recon.** Use the product once with capture on; for an API, script a minimal world. Write
   `targets/<t>/RECON.md`: where computed values appear, noise, error messages, surprises.
2. **Ledger** (recorder). `rules.json`: rules with provenance `observed | documented | inferred |
mined` and a reference. Documentation seeds rules; only a fixture confirms them. No status.
3. **Probe design** (recorder, then breaker in spec mode). In `probes.ts`:
   - designed probes: per rule, a case that triggers it and a boundary case; interacting rules
     combined; each probe creates its own starting state;
   - **the distribution D** the claim will speak about, as a seeded generator with its support
     written down in plain words (dimensions, ranges, frequencies), and dev probes drawn from it;
   - for screens: walkthroughs with full capture and breadth-first explorations;
   - then the breaker reads RECON, rules and documentation (no clone yet) and proposes inputs
     the generators never draw; widen D's support with what it finds before going on.
4. **Adapter.** `adapter.ts` implements `TargetAdapter`: `probes()`, `run(probe, side)` with the
   same code on both sides, `cloneEntry` (the clone's module; the harness runs it in its own
   process) and `recordedWith()` (the target's API and SDK versions).
5. **Policy**, before any clone code. `policy.json`: generated IDs canonicalised; every weakening
   (ignore, type, tolerance, perceptual, mask) carries its reason, decided from the target's own
   noise and semantics, never to make a clone pass.
6. **Record dev** (`npm run record <t>`): every probe twice, noise kept, scrubbed, locked. Commit
   fixtures and lock alone.
7. **Pre-register a holdout batch.** Size it from the claim: with no failure, 299 cases bound the
   failure rate below 1 % at 95 %; 473 still do so with one failure, and bound it below 1 % at
   99 % with none. Write `analysis-plan*.md` (batch IDs `hold-<name>-001…`, D, size, decision
   rule), draw the seed into `holdout-seed.json`, **commit both**, then record the batch.
   Prefer a **staged** batch (`stages` in `holdout-seed.json`, IDs `hold-<name>-s1-001…`): the plan
   then names each stage and the number of failures the claim tolerates.
8. **Build** (`harness/run-builder.sh <t>`). The builder works in the agent container on a copy
   with no holdout, no seed and no git history; only `clone/` comes back.
9. **Break** (`harness/run-agent.sh breaker <t> …`). The breaker reads the clone and proposes
   inputs to make it fail. Store them as `dev-brk-` probes (adversarial, never holdout), record,
   verify, and go back to 8 until a round finds nothing or the budget is spent. Their failure
   share is reported, never used as an estimate.
10. **Measure once.** Freeze the clone in a commit, run `npm run verify <t> -- --split holdout`
    once, apply the plan's decision rule and write the entry in `measurements.md`.
    For a staged batch: `npm run verify <t> -- --sequential hold-<name> --max-failures <k>` scores
    stage by stage and stops as soon as failures exceed k. Stopping only on failure leaves the
    success criterion unchanged, and the stages never scored stay fresh for the next clone.
11. **If the claim is rejected,** the batch is spent. Run `harness/run-analyst.sh <t> <batch>`
    right after the look; turn its findings into rules and `dev-` probes (designed after seeing
    failures, so they never certify); one more build pass; then a **new batch with a new seed
    and a new plan**, and back to 10. Never fix the failures and rescore the same batch.
12. **Variance**, when the budget allows: more builds from an empty server, each in its own
    worktree, each scored once on the claim's batch; write `variance.md`. Three builds show
    reproducibility; about 29 are needed to bound how often a build misses the bar below 10 %.
13. **Audit.** `npx tsx audit/meta.ts`: planted defects, recall per run; adjudicate the other
    findings and fix the real ones.
14. **Report.** `GAPS.md` with `## Scope` and `## Measured divergences` (the fidelity report quotes
    them), the claim with its scope in the README, and a test from a fresh clone (`npm ci`,
    `npm run check`, `verify --split all`).
15. **Lessons.** Append to `docs/lessons.md` what cost time and the rule that would have saved it.

## Rules that hold across steps

- **Learn only from spent sets.** Rules, probes and prompts may change after a batch's look;
  every new claim then needs a fresh batch. Every look is logged and counted per set.
- **Prefixes decide the split:** `hold-` is always holdout, `dev-` always dev, anything else by
  hash (a quarter to holdout, which carries no claim once looked at under several clone versions).
- **Costs are logged** in `timings.jsonl` (recording, verify, every agent run); quote them.

## Re-recording

Only with evidence that the target changed or the recording was wrong (replaying the original
shows it), never because the clone fails:
`npm run record <t> -- --rerecord <id> --reason "<evidence>"`, in its own commit whose message
carries the reason and the old and new hashes the command prints.

## Claims

Fidelity is stated as "N of M" with its bound, the set's status and the distribution it holds for.
Anything without a fixture is written: "Not covered by a fixture; behaviour inferred from
<source>; unverified."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs one agent headless inside the agent container, on a sandbox copy of the repository that
# holds no holdout, no audit material, no env or scrub files and no git history. The container
# sees only that copy (mounted at /work), not the host file system. The model credential comes
# from .agent.env through --env-file and is never written into the sandbox.
# Usage: harness/sandbox.sh <agent> <target> <task> [copy-back-dir]
# If copy-back-dir is given (for example targets/<t>/clone), that folder alone is copied back.
set -euo pipefail
agent="$1"
target="$2"
task="$3"
copy_back="${4:-}"
repo="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
image="software-clone-factory-agent"
credential="$repo/.agent.env"
stamp="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
log="$repo/targets/$target/logs/$agent-$stamp.jsonl"

command -v docker >/dev/null || { echo "refusing: docker is required (OrbStack or Docker Desktop)" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -f "$credential" ] || { echo "refusing: $credential is missing (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=...)" >&2; exit 2; }
docker image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1 || docker build -q -t "$image" -f "$repo/harness/docker/Dockerfile" "$repo" >/dev/null

sandbox="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/scf-sandbox-$agent-XXXX")"
egress="scf-egress-$agent-$stamp"
trap 'docker rm -f "$egress" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; rm -rf "$sandbox"' EXIT
"$repo/harness/make-sandbox.sh" "$repo" "$sandbox"

# An analyst may see one spent batch, and only one recorded as spent in measurements.md (its single
# look already taken). It goes under spent/<batch>/, out of every holdout path and pattern.
if [ -n "${SPENT_BATCH:-}" ]; then
  [[ "$SPENT_BATCH" =~ ^hold[a-z0-9-]*$ ]] || { echo "refusing: bad batch name $SPENT_BATCH" >&2; exit 2; }
  grep -q "\`${SPENT_BATCH}-001\`" "$repo/targets/$target/measurements.md" 2>/dev/null \
    || { echo "refusing: batch $SPENT_BATCH has no recorded look in measurements.md" >&2; exit 2; }
  spent="$sandbox/targets/$target/spent/$SPENT_BATCH"
  mkdir -p "$spent"
  find "$repo/targets/$target/fixtures/holdout" -name "${SPENT_BATCH}-[0-9]*.json" -exec cp {} "$spent/" \;
  jq --arg b "$SPENT_BATCH" '[.cases[] | select(.pass | not) | .id | select(test("^" + $b + "-[0-9]+$"))]' \
    "$repo/targets/$target/verify/holdout-verdict.json" >"$spent/failures.json"
fi

mkdir -p "$repo/targets/$target/logs"
# Hours of agent work must not vanish with the sandbox: the clone is copied back even when the run
# fails, and the run's status is returned at the end.
# Egress allowlist: the agent sits on an internal network with no route out; its only way out is
# a proxy container that lets through the model API (and the hosts a target lists in
# egress-allow.txt, such as its documentation) and refuses the rest, a code host included.
allow="api.anthropic.com"
if [ -f "$repo/targets/$target/egress-allow.txt" ]; then
  allow="$allow,$(grep -v '^#' "$repo/targets/$target/egress-allow.txt" | grep -v '^$' | paste -sd, -)"
fi
docker network inspect scf-internal >/dev/null 2>&1 || docker network create --internal scf-internal >/dev/null
docker run -d --rm --name "$egress" -e ALLOW="$allow" \
  -v "$repo/harness/docker/egress-proxy.mjs:/egress-proxy.mjs:ro" "$image" node /egress-proxy.mjs >/dev/null
docker network connect scf-internal "$egress"

status=0
docker run --rm \
  --env-file "$credential" -e RH_SANDBOX=1 \
  --network scf-internal \
  -e HTTPS_PROXY="http://$egress:3128" -e HTTP_PROXY="http://$egress:3128" -e NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1 \
  -e CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 \
  -v "$sandbox:/work" \
  "$image" \
  claude -p "Use the $agent subagent (Agent tool, subagent_type $agent) on target '$target' with this task, following .claude/agents/$agent.md: $task When it finishes, report its final answer verbatim." \
  --model claude-opus-5-5 \
  --permission-mode acceptEdits \
  --allowedTools "Bash Read Write Edit Grep Glob Agent WebFetch" \
  --output-format stream-json --verbose | tee "$log" | jq -rj 'select(.type == "assistant") | .message.content[]? | select(.type == "text") | .text + "\n"' || status=$?

# What the egress proxy refused, kept next to the run's log.
docker logs "$egress" 2>/dev/null | grep '^denied' >"${log%.jsonl}-egress-denied.log" || true
[ -s "${log%.jsonl}-egress-denied.log" ] || rm -f "${log%.jsonl}-egress-denied.log"

# The last line of the stream carries the run's totals: duration, turns, cost and tokens per model.
jq -c --arg agent "$agent" --arg stamp "$stamp" 'select(.type == "result")
  | {at: (now | todate), step: "agent", agent: $agent, log: ($agent + "-" + $stamp + ".jsonl"),
     seconds: (.duration_ms / 1000), turns: .num_turns, cost_usd: .total_cost_usd,
     usage: .usage, models: .modelUsage, ok: (.subtype == "success")}' "$log" \
  >>"$repo/targets/$target/timings.jsonl" || echo "warning: no result line in $log" >&2
# A build in a linked worktree is also logged in the main checkout, so its cost is never lost with it.
docker

run-agent.sh
run-analyst.sh
run-builder.sh

---
name: builder
description: Implements a target's clone under targets/<t>/clone/ until the dev fixtures pass. Cannot touch the evaluator and cannot see the holdout.
tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob
model: opus
---

You implement the clone of one slice of a closed-source product. The target's recorded behaviour
is the specification; your own opinion of how the product "should" work is not.

Read, in order: `targets/<t>/RECON.md`, `targets/<t>/rules.json`, `targets/<t>/adapter.ts` and the
drivers it imports (the exact requests and clicks the clone receives), `targets/<t>/policy.json`,
then the dev fixtures under `targets/<t>/fixtures/dev/`. Some fixtures record screens: an
accessibility tree, the boxes of visible elements (compared within the tolerance the policy
states), a small grey thumbnail (reported, never scored), the calls each step fired, the account
state a flow left behind, or a graph of every screen reachable by clicking. If `targets/<t>/failures.jsonl` exists, read it before proposing.

Loop:

1. Run `npm run verify <t>` first, to see the current state.
2. Pick the rule group with the most failing fixtures in `targets/<t>/verify/failures.json`.
3. Write down, in `targets/<t>/clone/NOTES.md`, the rule as you understand it from the fixtures and
   which fixtures you expect to flip. Then implement it.
4. Run `npm run verify <t>` again. Compare what flipped with your prediction.
5. After two failed attempts on the same rule, delete that part and rewrite it from the fixtures.
   After a third, write in NOTES.md that the rule statement itself looks wrong, and move on.

Constraints:

- Only write under `targets/<t>/clone/`. Fixtures, the lock, the policy, `rules.json`, `harness/`
  and `verify/` are read-only for you, and a hook blocks attempts. Do not look for ways around it.
- The clone never reads fixture files at runtime. Constants you learn from fixtures (static
  fields, defaults) are written in code.
- State lives in memory; `POST /__reset` must restore the seed; the same requests after a reset
  must give the same output (IDs included).
- Do not special-case a fixture by its values. If a behaviour only makes sense as a lookup table,
  say so in NOTES.md.
- `npm run check` must pass when you finish.

Finish with a short report: dev fixtures passing (from the verify output, not from memory), the
rules you could not make pass and why, and anything in the fixtures that contradicts `rules.json`.

10	Rules as read from the dev fixtures (checked offline against every logic fixture before coding):
11	
12	- Period: anchored on the start, same day of month (clamped), same time of day (PER-01).
13	- r = period end - proration date, P = period length, e = proration date - period start.
14	- No coupon: credit = -round_half_away(b r / P) on exact integers; flexible charge =
15	  Math.round(n (1 - e / P)) in floating point; classic charge = round_half_up(n r / P). 142 of 142
16	  single-item, no-coupon fixtures agree (PRO-01..04).
17	- A price change without a quantity bills quantity 1 (PRO-10).
18	- Coupons (DSC-04 / MOD-01): classic credit = -round((b - D) r / P) with D the discount the item got
19	  on the invoice that billed the period; flexible credit = -(round(b r/P) - sum round(D_k r/P)).
20	  These two differ by one cent in u-classic-off-once-q4 / u-flex-off-once-q4. Charge =
21	  prorated n minus the prorated discount of the new state (D2 = discounts applied to the new
22	  item alone). All single-coupon dev fixtures agree with these (several formulas are equivalent on
23	  the dev set).
24	- Discount allocation on invoice lines: discounts apply one after another in subscription order;
25	  percent-off per line is floor(base x pct), amount-off per line is floor(total x base / sum);
26	  the rounding remainder goes to the last line.
27	- once coupons: they discount the credited period (the credit carries them) and a once coupon passed
28	  to the preview discounts the remaining-time charge, but never the renewal lines and never appear
29	  in the invoice's `discounts` (DSC-05).
30	- A coupon passed to the preview replaces the subscription's discounts for the new state.
31	- discount_amounts on proration lines (lookup-like, observed only): classic = every invoice-level
32	  discount at 0; flexible = the first invoice-level discount at 0 (all of them for an immediate
33	  invoice), or, when the invoice has no discount, the discounts the line itself carries.
34	- Immediate invoice (always_invoice, or a classic interval change): created = clock time,
35	  period_start = period_end = clock time, auto_advance false, no next_payment_attempt. A classic
36	  interval change bills the new price for a full period from the clock time and has no
37	  remaining-time line. At the period end, or without any change, there is nothing to prorate and
38	  the preview is the renewal invoice.
39	- Flexible interval change: the new period is anchored on the current period start; a proration
40	  date at or past the new (shorter) period end is rejected (param null).

Method: each case replayed on the clone (`startCloneProcess` on a free port, `POST /__reset`
between cases, the adapter's `run` with the fixture's `input`), diffed with the harness's `diff`
and `blocking` under `policy.json`. Replaying the whole batch (473 cases) gives exactly the 7 IDs
of `failures.json` and no crash. Hypotheses were then checked by script against every dev fixture
(976) and every hold-b3 fixture, not only the failures. All 7 failures are classic billing mode.

## 1. Failing cases

| Case        | First differing fields                                | Expected => actual                                                                                                     | Category |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| hold-b3-086 | lines[0].amount (credit); subtotal, total, amount_due | -65291 => -65292; total 6397136 => 6397135                                                                             | A        |
| hold-b3-135 | lines[0].amount (credit); subtotal, total, amount_due | 0 => -148; total 1133640 => 1133492                                                                                    | A        |
| hold-b3-136 | lines[0].amount (credit); subtotal, total, amount_due | -80 => -89; total 26048730 => 26048721                                                                                 | A        |
| hold-b3-310 | lines[0].amount (credit); subtotal, total, amount_due | -22583154 => -22583165; total 588674245 => 588674234                                                                   | A        |
| hold-b3-282 | lines[1] (all fields), lines.total_count              | 2 lines => 3: clone inserts "Remaining time on Plan New after 17 Dec 2026" at 0 before the renewal "0 × Plan New" line | B        |
| hold-b3-300 | lines[1] (absent => present), lines.total_count       | 1 line (credit only, always_invoice) => 2: extra 0 "Remaining time on Plan New after 15 Apr 2027"                      | B        |
| hold-b3-393 | lines[1..3], lines.total_count                        | 3 lines => 4: extra 0 "Remaining time on Plan New after 05 Aug 2027", later lines shifted by one                       | B        |

In category B every total matches (the extra line is 0); only the line list differs.

## 2. Categories

### A. Classic credit: every discount of the billed line counts, even one the item got 0 from (4)

**Target rule.** In classic mode the unused-time credit is
`-round_half_away(net × r / P)` where `net` is the old item's amount `b` (unit × quantity) after
applying, in subscription order, _every_ discount that was on the subscription when the period
was billed, to that item alone: an amount-off in full (`min(amount, left)`), a percent-off as
`round(pct × left)`, clamped at 0. What share of each coupon the item actually got on the
multi-item first invoice does not matter, including a share of 0.

- hold-b3-086: forever $0.03 off, 3 items; the item got 0 of it on the first invoice (allocation
  0/2/1). `218750 × r/P = 65291.94`, `(218750 - 3) × r/P = 65291.05`: observed -65291.
- hold-b3-136: once $0.17 off, item share 0: `174 r/P = 89.14` vs `157 r/P = 80.44`: observed -80.
- hold-b3-310: once $0.09 and forever $0.02, both shares 0: observed -22583154 = `(b - 11) r/P`.
- hold-b3-135: once $15.07 off (share 0) then 77 % forever on an item of 1107: `1107 - 1507`
  clamps to 0, so the credit is 0; the clone, applying only the 77 %, gives -148.
- Checked on all 359 classic previews with a credit line (219 dev, 140 hold-b3): this rule fits
  359 of 359. The clone's reading ("only discounts with a non-zero share") fits 355 (fails the 4
  above). The "allocated share" reading fails 37 (dev: wide-101, wide-133, wide-136, wide2-027,
  wide2-051, wide2-140, wide2-198, wide2-248, wide2-276, wide2-280, wide2-281, wide3-026,
  wide3-046, wide3-088, wide3-108, wide3-164, wide3-170, wide3-257). Applying the coupons in
  reverse order fails 17, among them dev wide2-027/-040/-051/-084/-198/-281/-294, wide3-026/-189:
  subscription order is pinned by dev.

**Clone.** `clone/billing.ts:223` filters the billed discounts to `amount !== 0`, and
`billing.ts:229-234` computes `D` from that filtered list only. The comment at `billing.ts:227-229`
and NOTES.md pass 5 point 4 state "the prorated amount still uses the non-zero ones" as a finding.

**Dev evidence: not enough.** Only two dev cases have a coupon with a zero share on the credited
item, wide3-054 (100 % then 66 %) and wide3-249 ($3,492.68 then $0.04 on an item of 688), and in
both the first coupon already takes the whole item, so both readings give 0. The filter was not
required by any dev case; the simpler "apply all" reading fit every dev case equally well, so the
builder made an unforced choice that dev could not refute.

### B. Classic: no remaining-time line for a new item billed at 0 (3)

**Target rule.** In classic mode, when the changed item's new amount (unit amount × new quantity)
is 0, the preview has no "Remaining time" line: the credit line alone (plus the renewal lines,
where the "0 × Plan New" renewal line is kept). Flexible mode keeps a 0 "Remaining time" line.

- hold-b3-282, -393 (default behaviour) and -300 (always_invoice): quantity 0 with a new price,
  classic, no charge line.
- Over all classic previews with a credit line and no interval change (dev + hold-b3), a
  remaining-time line is present in 325 of 325 cases with new amount > 0 and in 0 of 3 with new
  amount 0. Classic 0-amount charge lines with a positive new amount are kept (dev
  dev-brk-pct100-half-classic, dev-t2-d-classic-_-end1/2-_, wide-019, wide-136, wide3-117, ...):
  the rule is about the item's amount, not the line's.
- Flexible quantity-0 changes all keep the 0 line: dev b-qty-zero, wide3-015,
  dev-brk-qty-to-zero-multi-always; hold-b3-007, -039, -118, -239, -297.
- Mirror of the existing credit-side behaviour (no credit line for an old item billed at 0,
  dev-brk-qty0-item, flexible only).

**Clone.** `clone/billing.ts:368-372` computes `n` but returns early only for `r2 <= 0`; the line
is pushed at `billing.ts:393` whatever `n` is, in both modes.

**Dev evidence: none.** No dev fixture changes a classic item to quantity 0 with prorations; every
dev quantity-0 change is flexible and keeps the line, which points the builder the wrong way.
`WIDE_DISTRIBUTION_V2` produces this case with probability about 0.3 × 0.4 × 1/21 × 0.85 ≈ 0.5 %
(1.4 expected among the 300 wide3 probes, 0 drawn; 3 among 473 here).

Untested within B: a classic quantity-0 change with coupons (whether a once coupon is then
spent, listed, or applied to the renewal).

## 3. Proposed rule statements (proposals only)

- **DSC-04 (correct):** "Classic mode: proration lines are not discountable. The credit is
  -round_half_away(net × r/P), where net is the old item's amount after applying every discount
  that was on the subscription when the credited period was billed, in subscription order, to that
  item alone: an amount-off in full, a percent-off as round(pct × what is left), never below 0.
  The share each discount got on the billing invoice is irrelevant, including a share of 0. The
  charge prorates first and subtracts the prorated discount after." Checked: 359/359 classic credits.
- **PRO-11 (new):** "Classic mode: when the changed item's new amount (unit amount × new
  quantity) is 0, the preview has no remaining-time line (default, create_prorations and
  always_invoice); the renewal still lists the item at 0. Flexible mode keeps a remaining-time
  line at 0. A 0 remaining-time line for a positive new amount (rounding, 100 % coupon) is kept in
  both modes." Checked: 325/325 + 3/3 classic, 8/8 flexible quantity-0.
- **ITM-01 / PRO-08 (extend):** add "An old item billed at 0 gets no credit line" (today only in
  NOTES pass 5; pinned by dev-brk-qty0-item, flexible only).
- **MOD-01 (extend):** add "and by the remaining-time line of a new item billed at 0 (PRO-11)".

## 4. Proposed dev probes (WideInput shapes)

All `kind: "wide"`, `interval: "month"`, a start mid-month, `offset` about half the period (so
the difference is many cents, not a rounding accident) unless stated.

Category A (classic; pair each with the same input in `flexible` as a control):

1. `items: [{amount: 1000, quantity: 1}, {amount: 1000000, quantity: 1}]`,
   `coupons: [{amount_off: 500, duration: "forever"}]`, `change: {item: 0, quantity: 2}`.
   Item 0's share is floor(500 × 1000 / 1001000) = 0; expected credit ≈ -250, not ≈ -500.
2. Same items, `coupons: [{amount_off: 500, duration: "once"}]` (once variant).
3. Same items, `coupons: [{amount_off: 1500, duration: "once"}, {percent_off: 50, duration: "forever"}]`:
   amount-off larger than the item, then a percent: expected credit 0 (clamp, then 50 % of 0).
4. Same items, `coupons: [{percent_off: 50, duration: "forever"}, {amount_off: 400, duration: "forever"}]`:
   zero-share amount-off after a percent (order check).
5. Three items `[{100, 1}, {500000, 1}, {500000, 1}]`, `coupons: [{amount_off: 3, ...}]`, offset 1
   and offset `len - 1`: the cent-level edge as in hold-b3-086.

Category B (classic; each also in flexible):

6. `items: [{amount: 2000, quantity: 2}]`, `coupons: []`, `change: {item: 0, amount: 5000, quantity: 0}`,
   behaviour null, `create_prorations`, `always_invoice` (three probes).
7. Same with `amount: null` (quantity-only change to 0).
8. Two items, change item 0 to quantity 0, behaviour null: the renewal keeps "0 × ..." and the other item.
9. Item 6 with `coupons: [{percent_off: 20, duration: "forever"}]` and, separately,
   `change.discount: {amount_off: 300, duration: "once"}`: pins discounts and once-coupon
   spending when no charge line exists (not covered by any fixture yet).
10. Control: classic `change.quantity: 1` with `offset: len - 1` (a positive amount whose charge
    rounds to 0: the line must stay).

## 5. Evaluator-side observations

- None of the 7 looks like an evaluator problem. `noise` is empty in all 473 fixtures; replaying
  the batch reproduces exactly `failures.json`; the differences are amounts the target computes
  differently (A) or a line the target omits (B), with no policy-masked field involved. Driver
  and `recorded_with` (API 2026-08-26.dahlia, stripe-node 22.6.2) are the same on both sides.
- Fixture `rules` tags do not name a rule that covers either category (no tag can, since neither
  rule exists); after adding PRO-11, the tagger should attach it to classic quantity-0 changes.
- Tooling, not verdicts: `harness/hooks/guard-oracle.sh` blocks the analyst's `Write` to `/tmp`
  (it allows analyst writes only under `analysis/`), although `analyst.md` asks for throwaway
  scripts in `/tmp`. It also matches the word "fixtures" in a Bash call's `description` field
  (`fixtures/?$`), so a harmless description such as "List spent batch fixtures" blocks the call.

## Summary

1. 7 failures of 473, all classic billing mode, two root causes; no evaluator problem found.
2. A, classic credit discounts (4: hold-b3-086, -135, -136, -310): Stripe applies every billed
   discount to the credited item, a zero-share one included; the clone drops zero-share ones.
3. A, confidence high: one rule fits 359/359 classic credits (219 dev, 140 hold-b3).
4. A, dev evidence insufficient: the only two zero-share dev cases cannot tell the readings apart.
5. B, classic charge for an item at 0 (3: hold-b3-282, -300, -393): Stripe omits the
   remaining-time line; the clone emits one at 0.
6. B, confidence high on the rule (325/325 and 3/3 classic, 8/8 flexible counter-cases);
   medium on its interaction with coupons (unobserved).
7. B, dev evidence absent: no classic quantity-0 change in dev; the flexible ones point the other way.
8. Proposals: correct DSC-04, add PRO-11, extend ITM-01/PRO-08 and MOD-01.
9. Ten probe designs in section 4 pin both categories without this batch.
10. Clone sites: `clone/billing.ts:223` (A) and `clone/billing.ts:368-372` (B).

export async function accountState(stripe: Stripe, subscription: string): Promise<Json> {
  const sub = await stripe.subscriptions.retrieve(subscription, { expand: ["items.data.price"] });
  const invoices = await stripe.invoices.list({ subscription, limit: 10 });
  const customer = typeof sub.customer === "string" ? sub.customer : sub.customer.id;
  const pending = await stripe.invoiceItems.list({ customer, pending: true, limit: 20 });
  return {
    status: sub.status,
    cancel_at_period_end: sub.cancel_at_period_end,
    cancel_at: sub.cancel_at ?? null,
    discounts: sub.discounts.length,
    items: sub.items.data.map((i) => ({
      amount: i.price.unit_amount,
      interval: i.price.recurring?.interval ?? null,
      quantity: i.quantity ?? null,
      period_end: i.current_period_end,
    })),
    // Oldest first, so that a new invoice appends instead of shifting every index.
    invoices: invoices.data.toReversed().map((inv) => invoiceView(inv)),
    // Prorations wait here until the next invoice; amounts sorted, since list order is by time.
    pending_items: pending.data
      .map((i) => ({ amount: i.amount, description: i.description ?? null }))
      .sort(
        (a, b) => a.amount - b.amount || (a.description ?? "").localeCompare(b.description ?? ""),
      ),
  };
}

    amount: l.amount,
